analysis.1:
Kickoff-day check, Wednesday Sep 9: all four picks confirmed healthy and the plan stands — LAC ×9, JAX ×9, DET ×7, PHI ×3. Real lines moved only at the margins: the Chargers eased from -10.5 to -9.5 (still ~80% at home over Brissett’s Cardinals — drift, not news), while Jacksonville firmed from -7.5 to -8.5 (~79%), so our two nine-deep cohorts are now nearly twins in win probability. Detroit (-7) and Philadelphia (-5.5) haven’t moved a tick in five days. Injury sweep is clean: Herbert healthy (the Biadasz loss at center is season-old news and priced in), the Jaguars filed no injuries, the Eagles enter healthy, and nothing has surfaced on Goff.

So the read is unchanged from the plan: expected survivors ~26 of 28, right on the count line, with a $125 buyback as the safety net on anything that misses. Nothing left to do before Sunday except lock all 28 picks on the pool site, glance at the Friday injury designations (Herbert, Lawrence, Goff, plus Washington’s side for the Eagles game), and check wind on the Philly game Sunday morning — the other three are domes or SoCal. If a QB from our four lands on the Friday report as questionable or out, shift that cohort’s weight toward Jacksonville and Detroit; do not unlock a hold team for Week 1.
analysis.2:
Friday, Sep 18 — injury sweep done (your Open-tap request): all four picks are clean where it counts. McCaffrey is healthy (the IR story was from an old season), Purdy/Herbert/Mayfield/Hurts all clean; McConkey (ribs) is trending OUT for the Chargers and the line already reflects it at -6.5. Board stands: SF ×9, LAC ×9, TB ×7, PHI ×3. Bills beat the Lions 41-31 Thursday — both are holds, nothing changes. Enter the Cohort C changes on Splash if you haven’t, then 🔎 Check Splash inputs.

Thursday, Sep 17 — PoolGenius Week 2 sheet is loaded (section 4). It lands exactly where the Tuesday read did: its Best Option is Tampa Bay (grade 100, 78%, 31% public) and its Second Best is Philadelphia (94, 73%, 11% public) — the two Cohort C landing spots. Baltimore grades only 64 despite 79% win odds because PG gives BAL the highest future value on the whole board (3.2): it agrees that spending the Ravens now is the expensive version. San Francisco is graded 89 at 85–89% but is the week’s most popular pick nationally (34%) with a -13.5 spread — fine as our anchor, no edge, no worry. Lines since Tuesday: SF -12.5 → -13.5, LAC -7 → -6.5, and Seattle slid again to -3.5 (PG has SEA at 62%) — the case for moving C off Seattle only got stronger. Tap ⚖ Compare for the full three-way read.

Tuesday update, Sep 15: real Week 2 lines are in and one of our four default legs is broken. Seattle opened -10 at Arizona and is now -4.5 — Sam Darnold is expected to MISS the game (glute tendon injury), and the market repriced the Cardinals after they beat our Chargers. A backup QB on the road at -4.5 is ~66%, nowhere near survivor grade: move Cohort C (entries 19–25) off Seattle. The clean landing spots: Baltimore -8.5 over New Orleans at home (~77%) and Tampa Bay -8.5 over Cleveland (~77%). BAL is the stronger team but burns a Wk-4 (vs TEN) and Wk-16 (vs CLE) anchor — and DK just made the Ravens the Super Bowl favorite (+750). Philadelphia -7 at Tennessee (~73%) is the no-anchor-burned alternative. My default: C → TB ×4 / PHI ×3 keeps every anchor in the bank and no game carrying more than 9 entries; C → BAL ×7 is the higher-percentage, higher-cost version. San Francisco firmed to -12.5 vs Miami (~86%) and stays the anchor on ×9.

The Chargers leg (×9, -7 vs LV) is fine but no longer premium — the line eased from -8.5 after the ARI loss and Ladd McConkey (ribs) is day-to-day. ~73% against a bad Raiders team is acceptable and Cohort B has no cheaper equivalent, so it holds. Two cautions: Detroit is an UNDERDOG Thursday night at Buffalo (+4.5) — nobody touches DET this week (all 28 still hold it, and BUF is a hold too — let that game pass). And the $1,000 buyback still showed UNPROCESSED on Splash as of Tuesday morning — entries 1–8 are listed Eliminated. Confirm the payment went through TODAY: Week 2 locks Sunday 1 PM ET, and 8 of our 28 don’t exist until it lands.
analysis.3:
Week 3 update, Thu Sep 24 — the pool reset around us. After Sunday’s carnage (TB 144, LAC 45, BAL 31 all lost) and the buybacks, 301 of 587 are alive and we are the biggest block at 28, ahead of vins 19, MC291 14, URAMALAKA 14 (didn’t rebuy), chcumming1 14 (bought back 10). FLPselver stayed at 5. All 28 of ours are back — at a price: $2,800 spent, $800 over the plan, with $175 / $200 / $225 rebuys still available in Weeks 3–5 if you want them. The count line for Week 3 is 21, so the goal this week is simple: a board that expects 21–22 survivors with no single game carrying more than 11.

The lines changed the plan. Kansas City is -10.5 AT Miami (~83%) — the best number on the board by a wide margin, against the worst team in football (+100000 to win the Super Bowl); Chiefs are healthy. San Francisco is -8.5 vs Arizona (~77%): Purdy limited (shoulder/toe) but McCaffrey full, both WRs Evans and Robinson missed Wednesday — still fine at home vs ARI, but it’s already used on 5 entries. Detroit, the planned Week-3 spend, is only -6.5 vs the Jets (~71%) with a banged-up secondary — usable, not premium. Seattle -7 at Washington (~73%) hinges on Darnold (limited Wed, decision Friday) — Daniels is out for Washington, so it’s a real option only if Darnold plays. The Giants (planned as filler) lost Jaxson Dart for the season — off the board. Buffalo -7 vs LAC is a premium hold; Green Bay Thursday is -4.5 with both starting tackles out — pass.

THE BOARD I’VE DEALT (by entry number, in the Entry sheet): Chiefs ×11 on the least-burned entries (#3–6, 8, 21, 22, 24, 25, 27, 28 — they’ve burned only cheap teams, so they can afford KC’s Week 9/11/18 value); 49ers ×10 on #1, 9, 10, 12, 13, 15, 17, 19, 20, 23; Lions ×7 on the entries that already spent SF or JAX+PHI (#2, 7, 11, 14, 16, 18, 26). Expected survivors ≈ 21.8, worst single game 11. If Darnold is confirmed Friday, SEA ×3–4 can replace Lions on #2/7/16/18 to cut the DET exposure — I’ll flag it after the Friday sweep. The pool will pile onto KC at -10.5 (expect 30%+); our SF and DET slices are the differentiation.
analysis.4:

With Thursday’s six Packers that is 14 of 28 down and 14 alive: 49ers ×6 (36-30), Chiefs ×6 (24-10) and Giants ×2 (12-7) all won. The pool went from 369 alive to 275 of 589 before rebuys: Seahawks 42, Packers 34, Saints 29, Panthers 14, Eagles 5. You are buying back 6 of the 14 at $175 ($1,050; season $3,850), so Week 4 starts with 20 alive. The six to revive are the ones that burned the least: #4, #10, #24 (only cheap teams plus the Packers), #2 and #7 (49ers, otherwise cheap) and #1 (Eagles + Packers). The eight that stay dead all burned the Seahawks or two premium teams. Week 3 is finalized on that basis; if you revive different entry numbers on Splash, tell me and I’ll re-map.

The field reset too. URAMALAKA is 27 of 42 (lost 15), FLPselver 11 of 28 (lost 17 — a $2,975 rebuy question), vins 12 of 21, MC291 14 of 14 (Chiefs ×14, three perfect weeks), KHART88 10 of 14, chcumming1 8 of 14, HARRIGAN000 8 of 13. At 20 we are second to URAMALAKA (27, before their rebuys) and ahead of MC291 (14) and vins (12).

Week 4 lines (DK via ESPN, Tuesday morning): Vikings -11.5 vs Miami and Ravens -11.5 vs Tennessee are the two anchors (~80% each). Miami just lost De’Von Achane for the season; Justin Jefferson (ankle sprain) is expected to play and the line moved UP a point on Monday anyway. Baltimore has both centers hurt long-term and Stanley (toe) is iffy, but the Titans are +50000 and it is -11.5 at home with light rain. Bills -7 vs New England (~70%, no injuries, Patriots just lost 35-6) and Seahawks -7 vs the Chargers (~70%; LAC is 0-3 and hasn’t scored 20 in six games) are the second tier. Everything else is -3.5 or less: the 49ers slid to -3 with Trent Williams carted off (neck) and Bosa out; Bears are on Case Keenum; Rams have Nacua questionable at Philly; Detroit is only -3.5 at Carolina Sunday night. No pick below the top four.

THE BOARD for 20 (Entry sheet): Vikings ×7 on #1, 4, 10, 14, 24, 27, 28 — Minnesota has almost no later value, so the most-burned entries spend them; Ravens ×6 on #3, 5, 6, 8, 19, 20 — at -11.5 the Ravens are worth spending now (Wk 16 -10 vs CLE stays as the backup and Wk 14 has the Lions); Bills ×4 on #9, 17, 22, 23; Seahawks ×3 on #2, 7, 12 (clean rosters that haven’t used them). Expected survivors ≈ 15.3 of 20, worst single game 7. Week 5 look-ahead: Patriots -8.5 vs LV and Lions -8.5 at ARI are the anchors and every entry still holds both, so the last buyback week is covered.
analysis.5:

The pool: 350 entered Week 4, 44 lost (Bills 16, Cardinals 14, Bengals 6, Saints 6), 306 alive before this week’s rebuys. Vikings were the chalk at 138, Ravens 82. Season buyback spend: $3,150.

The blocks: URAMALAKA 32 of 42 (lost 10 on BUF/ARI), FLPselver 16 of 28 (rebought 10, lost 5 on the Saints), MC291 14 of 14 (Vikings 9, Ravens 5 — still perfect), KHART88 13 of 14, vins 10 of 21 (lost 11 on CIN/BUF — the week’s big loser), chcumming1 9 of 14 (5 on Arizona), HARRIGAN000 9 of 13. Nobody has bought back yet this week; Week 4 rebuys are $200.

Week 5 is the LAST buyback week ($225). Lines (DK via ESPN, Tuesday): Cowboys -9.5 vs Tampa (THURSDAY 8:15 PM — picks lock Thursday), Bengals -7 at Miami, Texans -7 at Tennessee, Jaguars -6.5 vs Philadelphia in London, Lions -4.5 at Arizona, Patriots only -3.5 vs the Raiders. Injuries: Mayfield (dislocated thumb) is listed TBD but was out three weeks a week ago, Winfield is out — Tampa is thin; Dallas has Lamb full, Durant out. Cincinnati has Ja’Marr Chase in concussion protocol; Philadelphia is a mess (Barkley week-to-week, Jurgens, Smith, Goedert hurt), which is why Jacksonville is -6.5.

THE BOARD: all 16 on the COWBOYS, per the hedge plan — Tampa moneyline at about +400 needs a $720 stake to return the $3,600 that 16 rebuys would cost; size it to the price on Thursday and place it when you enter the picks. Dallas’s only later spot was Week 8 (-10.5 vs Arizona), and Steelers/Bengals/Patriots/Packers cover that week, so the burn is cheap. Texans are the Week 7 pair and stay untouched; Bengals keep Week 12. If you would rather split, Bengals ×8 at -7 with Miami +330 or so is the only other hedgeable spot of similar quality. Week 6 look-ahead (no lines posted yet; projections): Rams -13.5 vs Arizona, Patriots -9.5 vs Jets, Ravens -6.5 at Cleveland — first week a loss is final, so from there we spread: Rams 8 / Patriots 8.

analysis.7:
SUNDAY, Oct 25, 9 AM — lines re-pulled from DraftKings via ESPN. Movement since Friday: Jets -4.5 to -3.5 (Breece Hall upgraded to questionable, but the number went the wrong way), Rams -4.5 to -3.5 (Nacua still a pregame decision), Texans steady at -10.5 with both starting safeties (Pitre, Blankenship) and Montgomery out, Broncos steady at -4.5 with Surtain questionable. Pair odds now: Texans+Jets 48%, Texans+Broncos 49%, Rams+Jets 36%. Expected survivors about 5.4 of 12. The board stands; the only live decision is the Rams leg on #4, 12, 24 if Nacua is inactive.

Final designations: DENVER — Surtain QUESTIONABLE after a full week of limited practice (hasn’t played since Week 4) and that is an upgrade; Hufanga, Elliss and Badie are OUT, but Arizona is more banged up: Love, Wingard, Nolen and Gaines OUT, Budda Baker questionable. JETS/TEXANS — no new flags beyond Hall doubtful and Montgomery doubtful. Our games all kick 1:00 PM or later, so the real deadline is Sunday ~12:55 PM ET.

— — PREVIOUS: FRIDAY, Oct 23, 11 AM — FINAL Week 7 board, dealt on today's lines and the Friday injury reports. The market moved all week: Texans are now -10.5 vs the Giants (the only premium number on the board); the Rams fell to -4.5 at Las Vegas — Davante Adams is OUT 6-10 weeks (hamstring) and Puka Nacua is questionable (calf, DNP Friday); the Broncos sit -4.5 at Arizona; the Jets are -4.5 vs 1-5 Miami with the week's lowest total (Breece Hall doubtful); the 49ers collapsed to -2.5 at Atlanta (Deebo doubtful, Evans' Achilles flared — off our board); and Dallas is -4.5 AT Philadelphia with the Eagles on backup QB Tanner McKee — which also dents PHI's Week 13 value and raises what Denver is worth. The VIKINGS ARE OFF OUR BOARD entirely: every alive entry burned Minnesota in Week 4, so Monday's provisional SF+MIN legs were invalid and have been replaced.

THE BOARD for the 12 (two picks each, both must win): TEXANS + JETS on #6, 14, 17, 20, 23 (~50% joint) — the two cheapest burns in the pool, and it keeps Denver banked for the Week 13 anchor on the four entries that burned Philadelphia. TEXANS + BRONCOS on #3, 5, 27, 28 (~49%) — these four still hold PHI for Week 13, so Denver is spendable; Denver is on 10 days' rest with the defense carrying a slumping offense. RAMS + JETS on #4, 12, 24 (~39%) — the no-Houston hedge: if the Texans get shocked, these three keep the season alive; all three hold DEN and PHI for Week 13, and Buffalo/Seattle cover their Week 10 once the Rams are spent. Exposure: Texans 9, Jets 8, Broncos 4, Rams 3 — no single upset can end the season; expected survivors about 5.6 of 12. Sunday morning checklist: Houston's inactives (Montgomery doubtful), Nacua's status on the Rams leg, Surtain's status for Denver (ankle, missed last week), and the Thursday NE-CHI result's effect on the field (not available at this sweep).

— — PREVIOUS: Week 7 opening read, Mon Oct 19 — Sunday was the bloodbath the pool was built for. The Rams lost 18-16 to Arizona as 12.5-point favorites and the Colts lost 26-20 to Tennessee; the Ravens lost at Cleveland too. 138 of the 279 entries that went into the week are out (Rams 90, Colts 48) with the 49ers’ 38 still playing Monday night. Lines so far: Rams -7 at Las Vegas, Texans -7 vs the Giants, Vikings -5.5 vs Indianapolis, Jets -4.5 vs Miami, 49ers -4.5 at Atlanta; Broncos at Arizona, Chiefs at Seattle and Cowboys at Eagles are not posted yet (look-ahead Broncos -5.5). No team carries more than 8 of the 12, and the Rams coming off a loss at -7 at Las Vegas is the leg to watch. Expected survivors on the look-ahead numbers: about 5.5 of 12.
analysis.8:

analysis.10:

Still the thinnest number on our board — a divisional road game where a tie is a loss — but the QB gap is real and it’s the PoolGenius contrarian play (1% of the public).
